Founded in 1961 to spur economic progress and world trade, this 38-member intergovernmental forum unites high-income, advanced economies committed to democracy and the market economy. What is it?
OECD: Intergovernmental economic organisation. OECD members are highly developed countries with advanced economies typically considered efficient and high-income.

In early Christianity, this label — from a Latin word for "rustic" — was pinned on anyone in the Roman Empire who didn't follow an Abrahamic faith, often spotted by their taking part in ritual sacrifice. What's the term?
Which ruler, who reigned jointly with his half-brother Ivan V until 1696, founded the Russian Navy and became Russia's first Emperor in 1721?
Peter the Great: Tsar of Russia from 1682 to 1725.

Marrying his first cousin, the reigning British queen, at age 20, this royal consort championed educational reform and the abolition of slavery, and organized the Great Exhibition of 1851 — who was he?
Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha: Consort of Queen Victoria from 1840 to 1861.
Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
Third pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty, he waged 15 military campaigns and reigned 66 years — the longest recorded of any pharaoh — earning the title 'the Great.' Who was he?
Ramesses II: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1279 to 1213 BC.
An Italian neurobiologist who shared the 1986 Nobel for discovering nerve growth factor and served as a senator for life, she became the first Nobel laureate to turn 100 — who is she?

Serving as Ukraine's Defence Minister from 2023 to 2025 before becoming Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, this Crimean Tatar politician has co-chaired a Crimea diplomatic initiative since 2020 — who is he?
This Turkmen dictator gave himself the title 'Türkmenbaşy' — Leader of all Turkmen — and ruled the country from 1985 until his death in 2006. Who was he?
Saparmurat Niyazov: President of Turkmenistan from 1991 to 2006.
Lord of the desert and god of storms and chaos in ancient Egyptian religion, he murdered his own brother Osiris before being pursued for revenge by his nephew Horus — who is this god?
Set (deity): Egyptian god of the desert, storms, violence, and foreigners.
Nicknamed 'The White Death,' this Finnish marksman is credited with over 500 kills during the 1939-40 Winter War against the Soviets — who was he?

Born in Trinidad, this civil rights leader helped launch the Black Power movement while heading SNCC, then served as 'Honorary Prime Minister' of the Black Panther Party — and later took the name Kwame Ture. Who was he?
Described in its founding text as formless, eternal, and the 'Mother of the universe,' this East Asian philosophical concept's Chinese character means 'the way' or 'path' — what is it?
Tao: Philosophical concept native to China.
Sparked by tensions over Colombia's 1886 constitution and the Regeneración, this conflict pitted Liberals against a Conservative government from October 1899 to November 1902 — which conflict?
Thousand Days' War: Civil war in Colombia from 1899 to 1902. It would end three years later with the signing of the Treaty of Neerlandia and the Treaty of Wisconsin.
Once an actor who ran the film company Red Giant Movies, he served as Tamil Nadu's Deputy Chief Minister from 2024 to 2026 before becoming the state's Opposition Leader. Who is he?
Udhayanidhi Stalin: Indian politician and former actor.

Dubbed the 'Merchant of Death' after a 2003 UN report, this former Soviet military translator smuggled weapons from Eastern Europe to Africa and the Middle East before a 2008 Thailand sting — who is he?
One of the most popular presidents at his death in 1923, this Ohio newspaperman who built up the Marion Star saw his reputation later wrecked by exposed scandals — who was he?
Warren G. Harding: President of the United States from 1921 to 1923.
The longest-serving member of any democratic German parliament, this CDU politician served as president of the Bundestag from 2017 to 2021 — who was he?
Dismembered by the Titans and reborn, this figure from Greek myth was sometimes identified with an Orphic version of Dionysus and linked by Aeschylus to Hades — who is he?
Zagreus: Figure in Greek mythology. In the earliest mention of Zagreus, he is paired with Gaia and called the "highest" god, though perhaps only in reference to the gods of the underworld.
Which one below was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four. Thomas Carlyle (4 December 1795 – 5 February 1881) was a Scottish essayist, historian and philosopher.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four. C++ is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Danish computer scientist Bjarne Stroustrup.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Aryabhata is an astronomer. The claim that Nalanda used to be located in Kusamapura/Pataliputra also cannot be proven.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Michael Atiyah is a mathematician. Sir Michael Francis Atiyah (22 April 1929 – 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.
What is the atomic number of Tin?
Tin: Tin is a chemical element; it has the symbol Sn (from Latin stannum) and atomic number 50.
What is the atomic number of Titanium?
Titanium: Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
In what year was Alexander Hamilton born?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year was Ivan Pavlov born?
Ivan Pavlov: Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
In what year was Archimedes born?
Archimedes: Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
In what year did Kalpana Chawla die?
Kalpana Chawla: Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 – February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
In what year did Rosalind Franklin die?
Rosalind Franklin: Rosalind Elsie Franklin (25 July 1920 – 16 April 1958) was an English chemist and X-ray crystallographer.
In what year was Oxycodone discovered?
Oxycodone: It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Mikoyan MiG-29: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Which company manufactures BAE Systems Hawk?
BAE Systems Hawk: Hawker Siddeley. The BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.
Which country is Bombardier Challenger 600 series from?
Bombardier Challenger 600 series: Canada. At the end of 1975, Canadair began funding the development of LearStar 600, and then bought the design for a wide-cabin business jet in April 1976.
Who is credited with discovering Hassium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Hassium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Who is credited with discovering HD 209458 b?
HD 209458 b: Michel Mayor. It is sometimes informally called Osiris.
Who is credited with discovering Osmium?
Osmium: Smithson Tennant. Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
These mostly semiaquatic vertebrates are tetrapods that pointedly lack an amniotic membrane, splitting into just three living orders like the frogs and toads of Anura — what are they?
Amphibian are ectothermic, anamniotic, four-limbed vertebrate animals that constitute the class Amphibia.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.
Present in every living cell and abundant in liver and meats, this B vitamin acts as an enzyme cofactor and takes its name from the Greek for 'life' — what is it?
Biotin (also known as vitamin B7 and vitamin H) is one of the B vitamins - a group of essential dietary micronutrients.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.

Ranging from 9 to 20 centimeters long and known on the Italian mainland by a slightly different name, this Sicilian pastry features a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with a sweet ricotta cream — which pastry?
Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
First flown in 1998, this Chinese-built multirole combat aircraft features a delta wing and canard design and is nicknamed "Vigorous Dragon" — which fighter jet is it?

Chengdu J-10 (pinyin: Jian-Shi), also known as Menglong (pinyin: Menglong; lit. 'Vigorous Dragon'), is a Chinese medium-weight, single-engine, multirole combat aircraft with a delta wing and canard design.
Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.
This blood-feeding parasitic insect usually lives in human pubic hair and is thought to have diverged from a closely related gorilla parasite roughly 3.3 million years ago — what is it?
Crab louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Asian canid stands apart from true dogs: a convex rather than concave skull, no third lower molar, and single-cusped upper molars — once it roamed into Europe. What is it?
Dhole (dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.
Comprising around 50 species mostly found in the tropics, this fungal genus infects rye, wheat, barley, and other grasses, producing toxic alkaloids — name the group of fungi?
Ergot is a group of fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.

A bulbous Allium native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, this kitchen staple counts the chive, leek, and shallot among its cousins and was prized by ancient Babylonians and Egyptians — what is it?
Garlic (Allium sativum) is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.
This system of rules governs how a language is structured, covering everything from word order to the deeper study of sounds, meaning, and sentence formation — what is it called?
Grammar is the system of rules that governs how a natural language is structured and used, as evidenced by its speakers or writers.

Producer of Japan's first major turn-based role-playing video game, this Dutch-born American entrepreneur also secured console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game and resolved the licensing disputes that brought it to the Game Boy — who is he?
Henk Rogers is a Dutch-born American video game designer and entrepreneur.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.

Also known by the old names green vitriol and copperas, this heptahydrate salt dissolves in water to form a paramagnetic, octahedral aquo complex and is used medically to fight anemia — which compound is it?
Iron(II) sulfate (British) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4xH2O.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
Ranging from Patagonia to Bolivia during the Ice Age, this genus of giant ground sloths includes a type species that could weigh nearly four tonnes — which genus?

Megatherium (meg--; from Greek mga 'great' + theron 'beast') is an extinct genus of large ground sloths endemic to South America that lived from the Early Pliocene through the end of the Late Pleistocene.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.
A white crystalline solid built from two fused benzene rings, this aromatic compound is the main ingredient of traditional mothballs and has an odor you can smell at just 0.08 ppm. What is it?
Naphthalene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C10H8.
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Jointly built by Italy, the UK and Germany, this variable-sweep-wing combat aircraft comes in strike, electronic-warfare and interceptor variants — which jet?
Panavia Tornado is a family of twin-engine, variable-sweep wing multi-role combat aircraft, jointly developed and manufactured by Italy, the United Kingdom and Germany.
This class of compounds is defined by a direct single bond between two oxygen atoms, denoted R−O−O−R — what are they called?
Peroxide are a group of molecules with the structure ROOR, where each R represents a radical (a portion of a complete molecule; not a free radical) and the O's are single oxygen atoms.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.

This endogenous steroid sex hormone plays a central role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development, and also serves as a key metabolic intermediate for producing other steroid hormones — name the hormone?
Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.

Cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seeds, this yellow-flowered Brassica crop is the source of a low-toxicity oil marketed under a Canadian-coined name, and ranks as the world's third-largest vegetable oil source — what is it?
Caused by two strains of human herpesvirus and nicknamed 'sixth disease,' this common childhood illness brings a rapid fever that gives way to a pink rash within days — what's it called?
Roseola is an infectious disease caused by certain types of human herpes viruses.
With segmented bony armor, an upright posture, and a curling prehensile tail, these 46 species of tiny bony fish are cousins to the pipefishes and seadragons — what are they?
Seahorse (also written sea-horse and sea horse) is any of 46 species of small marine bony fish in the genus Hippocampus.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.

In 1976, this American engineer and inventor co-founded Apple Computer with his early business partner, later becoming known as one of the personal computer revolution's most important pioneers — who is he?
Steve Wozniak (born August 11, 1950), also known by his nickname Woz, is an American technology entrepreneur, electrical engineer, computer programmer, and inventor.
Every part of this Old World evergreen tree is poisonous except the fleshy red covering around its seed, and it's native across Eurasia and Northwest Africa — what tree species is it?
Taxus baccata is an Old World species of evergreen tree in the family Taxaceae.
Tetrapods have these digits at the end of each limb; horses walk on their very tips in what's called an unguligrade stance — what are they?
Toe are the digits of the foot of a tetrapod.
Native to cool climates across the Northern Hemisphere, this low shrub bears small, round, edible fruit of a deep blue color, and goes by several folk names depending on region — what's the species?
Vaccinium myrtillus is a holarctic species of shrub with edible fruit of blue color, known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry.
The first-ever recipient of the Nobel Prize in Physics, this German scientist discovered a form of electromagnetic radiation named after him in some languages — who was he?

Wilhelm Röntgen (27 March 1845 - 10 February 1923) was a German experimental physicist who produced and detected electromagnetic radiation in a wavelength range known as X-rays (known as Rntgen rays in many languages).
This Andalusi polymath built a model of the planets' motion, devised colourless glass, made reading lenses, and is even said to have attempted flight — who was this 9th-century inventor?
Abbas ibn Firnas: 9th-century astronomer and physician.
People with this anxiety disorder dread places they feel they can't safely escape — crowds, queues, public transit — and in severe cases become unable to leave home at all. What is it?
Agoraphobia: Anxiety disorder. Agoraphobia is believed to be due to a combination of genetic and environmental factors.
A succulent from the Arabian Peninsula, this popular potted plant stores a soothing gel of acemannan in its leaves — alongside a toxic compound called aloin. What is it?
Aloe vera: Species of plant. It is widely distributed, and is considered an invasive species in many world regions.

Born in Dunfermline, Scotland, and immigrating to Pittsburgh at age 12, this steel magnate gave away nearly 90 percent of his fortune after publishing an 1889 essay called 'The Gospel of Wealth' — who is he?
Andrew Carnegie: American industrialist and philanthropist (1835–1919)
In this severe blood disorder, the bone marrow stops producing red cells, white cells and platelets alike, and about half of all cases have no known cause — what condition is it?
Aplastic anemia: Disease causing insufficient blood cells of all types.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.

Baruch Goldstein: American-Israeli mass murderer (1956–1994). Goldstein was a supporter of Kach, a religious Zionist party that the United States, the European Union and other countries designate as a terrorist organization.
This natural science rests on five big themes — the cell, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis — to explain life itself. What field is it?

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Covered in coarse black hair but bare-faced, this great ape is humans' closest living relative according to fossil and DNA evidence, and lives in groups of up to 150 — which species?
Chimpanzee: Species of great ape. The chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
Sold as Catapres and Kapvay, this drug treats high blood pressure, ADHD, and drug-withdrawal symptoms, and can be delivered via a skin patch — what is it?
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Named for its 'skin wings,' this insect order sports pincer-like cerci on its abdomen and displays unusually attentive maternal care for its young — which insect?
Earwig: Order of insects. Damage to foliage, flowers, and various crops is commonly blamed on earwigs, especially the common earwig Forficula auricularia.

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.

Colloquially called squirting or gushing, this fluid is expelled from the Skene's gland near the urethra around the time of orgasm — and researchers stress it's physiologically distinct from coital incontinence. What is it?
Female ejaculation: Expulsion of fluid during orgasm.
This double-layered fold of skin covering the glans is attached by an elastic band called the frenulum and is typically fused in place at birth — what is it?
Foreskin: Retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis.
Naming his most famous pistol after his 17th patent — not for holding seventeen rounds, as many assume — this Austrian engineer got his design into Austrian service in 1982 — who was he?
This American chemist helped synthesize ten transuranium elements, dreamed up the actinide concept, and advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who shared the 1951 Nobel for that work?
Closely related to the llama, this wild South American camelid shares its range with a higher-altitude cousin, the vicuña — what is it?

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.
Distinct from a process that adds more cells, this one is an increase in the size of individual cells, like the uterus enlarging during pregnancy — what's it called?
Hypertrophy: Increase in the size of biological cells. Hypertrophy can lead to a relative increase in the volume of a tissue or organ, and contributes to the overall growth of an organism.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'hump,' this abnormal, excessive curving of the upper spine can result from osteoporosis, disc disease, or a condition common in teens called Scheuermann's disease — what is it called?
Kyphosis: Excessive convex curvature of the lower and middle spine.

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.
Genus name meaning 'horned' in Latin, this raptor nests in dense woodland edges but hunts over open ground, feeding mostly on voles — which bird?
Long-eared owl: Species of owl. The genus name, Asio, is Latin for "horned owl", and the specific epithet, otus, is derived from Greek and refers to a small eared owl.
Domesticated some 9,000 years ago in southern Mexico from a wild grass called teosinte, this tall stout grain was once planted beside beans and squash in the Three Sisters trio — what is it?
Maize: Species of grass cultivated as a food crop.

Born from a US-UK cooperative effort begun in the early 1970s to improve on a first-generation jump jet, this vertical-takeoff-capable attack aircraft has served the US Marine Corps plus Spanish and Italian navies — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II: Anglo-American VSTOL ground-attack aircraft.
Sold under brand names like Ritalin and Concerta, which stimulant medication is preferred as the first-line treatment for ADHD in children, while amphetamine is favored for adults?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
Described by Eric Kandel as the 'epic challenge' of biology, this multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system — what field is it?
Neuroscience: Scientific study of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This surgical medical subspecialty treats the ear, nose, and throat — organs connected via the Eustachian tube — earning its specialists the nickname 'ENT surgeons.' What field is it?
Otorhinolaryngology: Medical specialty of the head and neck.
From the Greek for 'the study of disease,' this medical field diagnoses illness largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — what is it?
Pathology: Study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
This self-limiting skin condition begins with a single “herald patch” before smaller scaly spots erupt days later, usually clearing up on its own within three months — which condition?
Pityriasis rosea: Skin disease. It usually lasts less than three months and goes away without treatment.
Used to disinfect skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can cause kidney problems and high blood sodium if applied to large wounds, and comes as a liquid, ointment, or powder — what is it?
Povidone-iodine: Antiseptic solution. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
